readings.title: Is a Man Profitable to El?
readings.subtitle: Eliphaz Accuses Job of Wickedness
readings.text: [Job 22:1] Then Eliphaz the Tĕmanite answered and said, [2] “Is a male profitable to <dn>El</dn>? For he who is wise is profitable to himself. [3] Is it a pleasure to <dn>Shaddai</dn> that you are righteous? Or is it gain to <dn>Him</dn> that you make your ways perfect? [4] Does <dn>He</dn> reprove you for fear of you? Does <dn>He</dn> enter into right-ruling with you? [5] Is not your evil great, and your crookednesses without end? [6] For you have taken a pledge from your brother for naught, and stripped the naked of their garments. [7] You have not given the weary water to drink, and you have withheld bread from the hungry. [8] But the man of power – the earth is his, and the accepted one dwells in it. [9] You have sent widows away empty, and the arms of the fatherless are crushed. [10] Therefore snares are all around you, and sudden dread troubles you, [11] or darkness, so that you do not see; and a flood of water covers you.”

readings.title: The Path of the Wicked
readings.subtitle: Eliphaz Claims Job Walks the Old Way
readings.text: [Job 22:12] “Is not <dn>Eloah</dn> in the height of the heavens? And see the highest stars, how high they are! [13] And you say, ‘What does <dn>El</dn> know? Does <dn>He</dn> judge through the dark cloud? [14] Thick clouds cover <dn>Him</dn>, so that <dn>He</dn> does not see, and <dn>He</dn> walks about the circuit of the heavens.’ [15] Do you observe the path of old which wicked men have trodden? [16] Who were cut down before their time? Their foundation was poured out like a river. [17] Who said to <dn>El</dn>, ‘Turn aside from us!’ And what could <dn>Shaddai</dn> do to them? [18] Yet <dn>He</dn> filled their houses with good! But the counsel of the wicked has been far from me. [19] The righteous see it and are glad, and the innocent mock them, [20] saying, ‘Truly our adversaries are cut off, and the fire has consumed their remnant.’ ”

readings.title: Yield Now and Be at Peace
readings.subtitle: A Call to Repentance
readings.text: [Job 22:21] “Now be of service to <dn>Him</dn> and be at peace; thereby good shall come to you. [22] Please receive the Torah from <dn>His</dn> mouth, and lay up <dn>His</dn> words in your heart. [23] If you return to <dn>Shaddai</dn>, you shall be built up; put perversity far from your tents. [24] Then place gold in the dust, and the gold of Ophir among the stones of the brooks. [25] And <dn>Shaddai</dn> shall be your gold, and your silver, heaps of it. [26] For then you shall delight yourself in <dn>Shaddai</dn>, and lift up your face to <dn>Eloah</dn>. [27] You shall make your prayer to <dn>Him</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> shall hear you, and you shall pay your vows. [28] And you shall decree a matter and it shall be established for you, and light shall shine on your ways. [29] When they have made low, then you shall say, ‘Lift up!’ And <dn>He</dn> saves the one with lowly eyes. [30] <dn>He</dn> delivers one who is not innocent; yes, he shall be delivered by the cleanness of your hands.”

readings.title: Oh, That I Knew Where to Find Him
readings.subtitle: Job Seeks a Hearing Before God
readings.text: [Job 23:1] Then Iyoḇ answered and said, [2] “Even today my complaint is bitter; my hand is heavy because of my groaning. [3] Oh, that I knew where to find <dn>Him</dn>, that I might come to <dn>His</dn> seat! [4] I would set my right-ruling in order before <dn>Him</dn>, and fill my mouth with arguments. [5] I would know the words <dn>He</dn> would answer me, and understand what <dn>He</dn> would say to me. [6] Would <dn>He</dn> contend with me in <dn>His</dn> great power? No! <dn>He</dn> would take note of me. [7] There the upright could reason with <dn>Him</dn>, and I would be delivered forever from my Judge. [8] See, I go forward, but <dn>He</dn> is not there; and backward, but I do not perceive <dn>Him</dn>; [9] on the left hand when <dn>He</dn> works, but I do not see <dn>Him</dn>; <dn>He</dn> turns to the right hand, but I do not see <dn>Him</dn>.”

readings.title: He Knows the Way That I Take
readings.subtitle: Confidence in Integrity, Fear of Sovereignty
readings.text: [Job 23:10] “For <dn>He</dn> knows the way that I take. When <dn>He</dn> has tried me, I shall come forth as gold. [11] My foot has held fast to <dn>His</dn> steps; I have guarded <dn>His</dn> way and did not turn aside. [12] I have not yielded from the command of <dn>His</dn> lips; I have treasured the words of <dn>His</dn> mouth more than my daily portion. [13] But <dn>He</dn> is in one mind, and who turns <dn>Him</dn> back? And <dn>His</dn> being desires it, and <dn>He</dn> does it. [14] For <dn>He</dn> completes my portion, and many such are with <dn>Him</dn>. [15] Therefore I am troubled at <dn>His</dn> presence; when I consider this, I am afraid of <dn>Him</dn>. [16] For <dn>El</dn> has made my heart soft, and <dn>Shaddai</dn> has troubled me; [17] because I was not cut off from the presence of darkness, and <dn>He</dn> has covered thick darkness from my face.”

readings.title: Why Does Shaddai Not Set Times?
readings.subtitle: The Oppression of the Poor
readings.text: [Job 24:1] “Why are times not hidden from <dn>Shaddai</dn>? And why do those who know <dn>Him</dn> not see <dn>His</dn> days? [2] They move landmarks; they seize flocks and feed them. [3] They drive away the donkey of the fatherless; they take the widow’s ox as a pledge. [4] They turn the needy out of the way; the poor of the earth hide themselves together. [5] See, as wild donkeys in the wilderness, they go out to their work, searching for food. The desert yields food for them and for their children. [6] They harvest their fodder in the field, and they glean in the vineyard of the wrong. [7] They spend the night naked, without a garment, and have no covering in the cold. [8] They are wet with the showers of the mountains, and embrace the rock for want of shelter. [9] They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge from the poor. [10] They go naked, without a garment; and they take away the sheaf from the hungry. [11] They press out oil within their walls; they tread winepresses, yet suffer thirst. [12] Men groan from the city, and the throat of the wounded cries out, yet <dn>Eloah</dn> does not ascribe folly to it.”

readings.title: Rebels Against the Light
readings.subtitle: The Secret Crimes of the Wicked
readings.text: [Job 24:13] “They are of those who rebel against the light; they do not know its ways nor abide in its paths. [14] The murderer rises with the light; he kills the poor and needy; and in the night he is like a thief. [15] And the eye of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye sees me’; and he disguises his face. [16] In the dark they break into houses which they marked for themselves in the daytime; they do not know the light. [17] For the morning is the same to them as the shadow of death; if one recognizes them, it is the terrors of the shadow of death.”

readings.title: Swift on the Face of the Waters
readings.subtitle: The End of the Wicked
readings.text: [Job 24:18] “He is swift on the face of the waters; their portion is cursed in the earth; he does not turn into the way of the vineyards. [19] Drought and heat consume the snow waters, so does She’ol those who have sinned. [20] The womb forgets him, the worm feeds sweetly on him; he is remembered no more. And unrighteousness is broken like a tree. [21] He feeds on the barren who gives no birth, and does no good to the widow. [22] But <dn>He</dn> draws the mighty away with <dn>His</dn> power; <dn>He</dn> rises up, but no one is sure of life. [23] <dn>He</dn> gives him safety, and he leans on it; yet <dn>His</dn> eyes are on their ways. [24] They are exalted for a little while, then they are gone. And they are brought low; they are gathered in like all others, and cut off like the heads of grain. [25] And if it is not so, who proves me a liar, and makes my speech worth naught?”

readings.title: How Can Man Be Righteous?
readings.subtitle: The Majesty of God and Impurity of Man
readings.text: [Job 25:1] Then Bildad the Shuḥite answered and said, [2] “Rule and fear belong to <dn>Him</dn>; <dn>He</dn> makes peace in <dn>His</dn> high places. [3] Is there any number to <dn>His</dn> armies? And on whom does <dn>His</dn> light not rise? [4] How then is man righteous with <dn>El</dn>? Or how is he clean who is born of a woman? [5] See, even the moon does not shine, and the stars are not clean in <dn>His</dn> eyes; [6] how much less man, a maggot, and the son of man, a worm?”
